comments.author: gigatexal
comments.story_title: Designing database: split into different tables or group them together?
comments.why_zh: 围绕访问模式创建 DynamoDB schema 的演讲
comments.quote_zh: re:Invent 上几乎每年都有一场很棒的演讲，讲怎么创建 DynamoDB schema
comments.text_zh: 如果你采用单表设计，在数据库支持的情况下可以用 filtered indexes 来加速查询，而不必用 where 子句做逐行扫描。个人觉得这活儿适合 DynamoDB，不过它本身就是另一头巨兽。你必须事先清楚会对数据库做哪些查询，因为这决定了你如何设计。re:Invent 上几乎每年都有一场很棒的演讲，讲怎么创建 DynamoDB schema（[VIDEO]）。我会按理论先做规范化，再根据性能需要做反规范化。
comments.text: If you go single table you can use filtered indexes if your database supports it to speed up queries instead of having to do a row by row search with a where clause. Personally this seems like a job for DynamoDB but that’s a whole beast unto itself. You must know the queries you will do to the database before hand as that guides how you craft it. There’s an amazing talk at reinvent that is given almost every year on creating a DynamoDB schema ( [VIDEO] ) I would normalize as the theory says and then denormalize as performance requires it.

comments.why_zh: 解释如何在键值存储中高效建模关系型数据
comments.text_zh: 我在新项目里见过这种做法，效果非常好。如果你的数据访问模式确实是关系型的（查询路径多种多样），那它大概不是合适的工具，但很多应用都可以按 DDB 擅长的方式建模。强烈推荐观看：[VIDEO] 这个演讲解释了如何为键值存储高效地建模关系型数据。
comments.text: I've seen this done for new projects, and it works really well. If your data access patterns are truly relational (varied lookup paths) then it is probably not the right tool, but many apps can be modeled in a way that DDB handles well. Highly recommended viewing: [VIDEO] this talk explains how relational data can be efficiently modeled for key-value stores.

comments.author: mabbo
comments.why_zh: 那场演讲让亚马逊工程师对 DynamoDB 数据层设计惊叹不已
comments.text_zh: 几年前 Rick Houlihan 做过一场演讲，讲的是如何为使用 DynamoDB 的应用回头设计数据。我把它给很多人看，最常见的反应——其中大多数是运维使用 DynamoDB 的服务的亚马逊 SDE——是“卧槽，这是什么魔法？！”[VIDEO] 人们用 Dynamo 时犯的最大错误之一，就是以为它只是一个没有关系的关系型数据库。并不是。它是个了不起的系统，但要想充分享受它的好处，需要大量深入的知识，而且往往要求你在前期就把数据层设计得非常好。其实我不建议把它用在一个设计还没有基本稳定下来的系统上。但用对了的话，它就是一头性能惊人的数据存储猛兽。
comments.text: Rick Houlihan did a talk a few years ago about designing the data later for an application using dynamodb. The most common reaction I get from people I show it to- most of them Amazon SDEs who operate services that use Dynamodb- is "Holy shit what is this wizardry?!" [VIDEO] One of the biggest mistakes people make with dynamo is thinking that it's just a relational database with no relations. It's not. It's an incredible system, but it requires a lot of deep knowledge to get the full benefits, and it requires you, often, to design your data layer very well up-front. I actually don't recommend using it for a system that hasn't mostly stabilized in design. But when used right, it's an incredibly performant beast of a data store.

This can generally resolve a lot of the problems inherent in the need for relations. This might not be useful advice for everyone, but I can highly recommend this youtube video on DynamoDB data modelling: [VIDEO]

comments.author: forgingahead
comments.story_title: Building a scalable e-commerce data model
comments.why_zh: 关于 NoSQL 数据建模权衡的视频
comments.quote_zh: 这个视频讲这个话题很好
comments.text_zh: 如果我能给个建议——别折腾了。就像另一位评论者指出的，你为平台存储的许多数据本身就包含关系；至于那些你想保留完整数据哈希的部分，直接用 Postgres 的 jsonb 就好。等到收入达到几百万时，你再考虑为了某些效率原因把部分数据拆到文档存储方案里，但这绝不是必须的。这个视频讲这个话题很好：[VIDEO]
comments.text: If I may share some advice - don't bother. As another commenter pointed out, relationships are inherent in a lot of the data you'll store for your platform, and for those elements that you'd like to keep the full data hash, just use jsonb in Postgres. Once you're at several million in revenue, then you can think about splitting off some parts of your data into document storage solutions for certain efficiency reasons, but that is by no means necessary. This is a great video on the topic: [VIDEO]

comments.author: isbvhodnvemrwvn
comments.story_title: A minimalistic Python wrapper to AWS DynamoDB
comments.why_zh: 展示键如何能在 DynamoDB 中处理关系型数据
comments.quote_zh: 这个 re:Invent 视频很好地展示了这一点
comments.text_zh: 问题在于，键可以在不同程度上用来处理关系型数据（这个 re:Invent 视频很好地展示了这一点：[VIDEO]）。但人们忽略的是，为了不搬起石头砸自己的脚，你必须拥有稳定、已知且符合 DynamoDB 约束的访问模式。DynamoDB 的文档甚至也这么说：[LINK] 这意味着，对于 Amazon 的购物车来说这是个很好的用例，因为那里能做的创新有限，而且它非常契合；但对于一个需求不断变化、带关系型数据的新应用来说，这是一个糟糕透顶的选择，你会为此付出惨重代价。
comments.text: The issue is that the keys can be used to various extent to handle relational data (this re:Invent video shows this well: [VIDEO] ). What people miss though is that in order to not shoot themselves in the foot, you have to have stable, known access patterns which meet the constraints of DynamoDB. Even the documentation of DynamoDB says so: [LINK] This means that it's a good use case for shopping cart of Amazon since there's limited innovation possible there and it fits the bill nicely, but for a new application with relational data where the requirements change all the time - it's a terrible, terrible choice for which you will pay dearly.
